title: Integrative multi-omics and machine learning identify the SPI1-METTL16-PLIN4 axis as a candidate driver of steatosis in HepG2 cells.
authors: Xiao, Zhizhou; Bian, Huawei; Huang, Ying
one_liner_zh: 该文通过多组学与机器学习识别NAFLD中SPI1-METTL16-PLIN4轴，虽含SPI1与METTL16启动子结合的ChIP验证，但核心是脂质代谢表型与m6A调控，非TF-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，仅边缘相关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is a prevalent metabolic disorder with limited therapeutic options. This study aimed to identify potential regulators and explore their functional roles in a cellular model of NAFLD. METHODS: WGCNA was performed on the hepatic transcriptomic dataset GSE126848 (31 NAFLD vs. 26 controls), followed by integration with serum proteomic data from 12 NAFLD patients and 12 healthy controls. Hub genes were prioritized using three machine learning algorithms. Functional validation was conducted in a HepG2 cellular steatosis model induced by high fructose (3.2 g/L) and oleic acid (400 muM) for 48 h. Lipid accumulation was assessed by Oil Red O staining and triglyceride/total cholesterol measurement. Inflammation was evaluated by TNF-alpha and IL-6 secretion (ELISA), and oxidative stress by ROS levels (flow cytometry). The binding interaction between METTL16 and PLIN4 mRNA was validated by RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP)-quantitative PCR. METTL16-mediated m6A modification of PLIN4 was assessed by Methylated RIP (MeRIP)-quantitative PCR. Transcriptional regulation of METTL16 by SPI1 was examined by chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) and dual-luciferase reporter assays. RESULTS: Integrative analysis identified PLIN4 as a core hub gene. PLIN4 was upregulated in the HepG2 steatosis model (P < 0.001). PLIN4 knockdown alleviated lipid droplet accumulation (P < 0.001), reduced TNF-alpha and IL-6 secretion (P < 0.01), and decreased ROS levels (P < 0.001) in fructose/oleic acid-treated HepG2 cells. Mechanistically, METTL16 mediated its m6A modification to enhance PLIN4 mRNA stability. Furthermore, SPI1 was found to transcriptionally activate METTL16 by binding to its promoter (P < 0.001). PLIN4 re-expression partially reversed the protective effects of SPI1 knockdown on lipid accumulation (P = 0.01), inflammation (P < 0.05), and oxidative stress (P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: This study identifies the SPI1/METTL16/PLIN4 axis as a potential regulatory mechanism contributing to in vitro steatosis, inflammation, and oxidative stress in steatotic HepG2 cells.
abstract_zh: 背景：非酒精性脂肪性肝病（NAFLD）是一种常见的代谢性疾病，治疗选择有限。本研究旨在识别潜在调控因子，并探讨其在NAFLD细胞模型中的功能作用。方法：对肝转录组数据集GSE126848（31例NAFLD vs. 26例对照）进行WGCNA分析，随后与12例NAFLD患者和12例健康对照者的血清蛋白质组数据整合。使用三种机器学习算法优先排序核心基因。在高果糖（3.2 g/L）和油酸（400 μM）诱导48小时的HepG2细胞脂肪变性模型中进行功能验证。通过油红O染色和甘油三酯/总胆固醇测量评估脂质积累。通过TNF-α和IL-6分泌（ELISA）评估炎症，通过ROS水平（流式细胞术）评估氧化应激。METTL16与PLIN4 mRNA之间的结合相互作用通过RNA免疫沉淀（RIP）-定量PCR验证。METTL16介导的PLIN4 m6A修饰通过甲基化RIP（MeRIP）-定量PCR评估。SPI1对METTL16的转录调控通过染色质免疫沉淀（ChIP）和双荧光素酶报告基因实验检测。结果：整合分析将PLIN4确定为核心枢纽基因。PLIN4在HepG2脂肪变性模型中上调（P < 0.001）。PLIN4敲低减轻了果糖/油酸处理的HepG2细胞中的脂滴积累（P < 0.001），降低了TNF-α和IL-6分泌（P < 0.01），并减少了ROS水平（P < 0.001）。机制上，METTL16介导其m6A修饰以增强PLIN4 mRNA稳定性。此外，发现SPI1通过结合其启动子转录激活METTL16（P < 0.001）。PLIN4重新表达部分逆转了SPI1敲低对脂质积累（P = 0.01）、炎症（P < 0.05）和氧化应激（P < 0.001）的保护作用。结论：本研究将SPI1/METTL16/PLIN4轴确定为脂肪变性HepG2细胞中体外脂肪变性、炎症和氧化应激的潜在调控机制。
